name_en: Taihu-type rock 青莲朵 'Blue Lotus Bud'
place_text: in 蒨园, in the middle of the entrance court inside the gate (S1165: 陈列于蒨园之迎门庭院正中; repo CC03-05 from S05: west of 朗润斋, inside the garden gate); one of the eight views of 蒨园 (1753)
quote: Summary: the Southern Song 芙蓉石 of the 德寿宫 at Hangzhou (S1165: over 800 years old), found by Qianlong on his southern tour of 1751, sent to Beijing the next year, set in 蒨园 of 长春园 and named 青莲朵; in the Republic moved with other YMY rocks to 中山公园 (about 1915 per S1163; 1925 purchase per S409); in the 中国园林博物馆 since 2013 (S1165, S409). Size (S1165): 145 cm high, 228 cm long, up to 123 cm thick.
note: NOT in its 1860 place: now in the 中国园林博物馆 (Beijing, 丰台). Its stele 梅石碑 (the 1767 copy) stands on the PKU campus south-west of 临湖轩 and north-west of 俄文楼, under an earth mound (moved there in 1992, S1163). Date of the move to 中山公园 (1915 or 1925) to settle. For the model: one low, long single rock (1.45 x 2.28 m) on a base in the middle of the 蒨园 entrance court.

name_en: Fangshan rock 青云片 'Blue Cloud Slice' (not a Taihu rock)
place_text: before 时赏斋 (YM34-04) at 别有洞天
quote: Summary: one of two rocks of the Ming painter 米万钟, quarried at 房山 south-west of Beijing; Qianlong took the large one (青芝岫) to 清漪园 乐寿堂 and the small one, 青云片, to 时赏斋 in the YMY; cleared from the ruins and set up in 中山公园 in 1925, west of the long gallery west of 来今雨轩; Qianlong's 青云片 and eight poems remain on it.
note: NOT in its 1860 place: 中山公园. S408 decoded as GB18030 and read. A grey Fangshan limestone, not Taihu. Scene YM34 别有洞天 (parent of 时赏斋 YM34-04).

name_en: Taihu-type rock with Qianlong's poem 假山 of the 16 views of 狮子林
place_text: in 狮子林 (Changchun Yuan); the poem is one of the sixteen views, 假山
locator: S1164 (新华网 via 中国日报网, 2020-09-09)
quote: Summary: on 8 Sep 2020 a Taihu rock on a rectangular 须弥座, carved with Qianlong's verse for 狮子林, was given back to the park from a courtyard in 西城区; authenticated by the Beijing heritage bureau's board; to be shown in the returned-relics area at 天心水面 (QC26).
note: NOT in its 1860 place. The first returned Taihu rock bearing a poem. Rocks of 狮子林 were a rock-labyrinth after Suzhou's 狮子林: strong evidence for dense Taihu rockwork in CC13.

place_text: 凤麟洲: the rockwork at the south-east corner of the west island is original
quote: Summary: at 凤麟洲 the rockwork of the west island's south-east corner survives in its original state.
note: In its 1860 place (if the 1809-17 rebuilding of Qichun is taken as the base). Rocks only, no plants named.

name_en: rock hill (rockery) of 紫碧山房
place_text: 紫碧山房, the north-west corner: a rock garden about 15 m high, the highest point of the YMY
quote: Summary: 紫碧山房 has a rock garden 15 m high, the highest point of the gardens (no method given).
note: Today's rockery, in place; dug in the 13th Five-Year period (2016-20) (search snippet, national heritage administration reply). Height unmeasured by the repo.

name_en: wood and lawn, trees placed by size and tint
place_text: the parts near the embassy's lodging: ground broken into hill and dale, wood and lawn 'like Richmond park'; banks thrown up irregularly; rocky promontories into a lake; valleys choked with wood, others cultivated; trees placed by size and by the tint of their foliage
quote: broken into hill and dale, and diversified with wood and lawn ... Bold rocky promontories are seen jutting into a lake, and vallies retiring, some choaked with wood, others in a state of high cultivation ... the tints of their foliage seemed also to have been considered
note: Barrow was at the YMY Aug-Oct 1793, saw only parts near the lodging and the audience hall ('a stolen glance'). 'lawn' in 1790s English = open grass, not a mown lawn. Fields inside the garden ('high cultivation') agree with the rice and farm scenes.

name_en: flower garden enclosed by a brick wall
place_text: at the audience hall (the throne inscribed 'true, great, refulgent, splendor' = 正大光明): a flower garden enclosed by a fine brick wall
quote: a brick wall enclosing the flower garden, which, perhaps, in no respect is exceeded by any thing of the sort in England
note: Which side of the hall not said. The hall is fixed by the plaque Barrow translates.

place_text: Barrow p.130 quoting Macartney: lakes overspread with lotus
quote: In many places the lake is overspread with the Nenuphar or lotus (nelumbium)
reject_reason: the passage is Macartney on the gardens of Jehol (避暑山庄), not the YMY
note: Recorded so it is not reused for the YMY by mistake.

name_en: rocks and imported 'mountains' round the lake behind the audience hall
place_text: beyond the first throne hall: an artificial lake ringed by rocks and imported 'mountains', with a sanded road along it; a bridge over its feeding canal leads to a third throne hall
quote: un lac artificiel entouré de rochers et de montagnes rapportés, lequel était côtoyé par une route sablée
note: The lake = 前湖 between 正大光明 and 九洲清晏, as in M'Ghee (S242 pp.204-205). Varin compiled from the French officers' reports: B.
